reading: A square outline has an empty interior and two single-colour marks sit outside it. The interior is cut into four quadrants. The quadrant nearest each mark, and the quadrant diagonally opposite it, take that mark's colour.

slots.region: interior of the one rectangular outline, split into 4 equal quadrants
slots.colour source: the two isolated marks outside the outline
slots.rule: the quadrant nearest a mark and its diagonal opposite get that mark's colour (checkerboard of the two colours)

why: the interior is a 2x2 checkerboard of quadrants; the quadrant on a mark's side always carries that mark's colour

reading: A strip of vertical colour bars is a key giving a top-to-bottom colour order. One shape already appears stacked in some of those colours. The shape is copied in every key colour, stacked vertically in key order and aligned with the existing copies, and the key is erased.

slots.key: the multi-colour bar block; its column order left to right is the stacking order top to bottom
slots.unit: the repeated shape (same shape in every existing colour)
slots.placement: copies for the missing key colours go directly above or below the existing ones, so the stack follows key order

why: the output column of shapes reads the key colours in order, each copy has the same shape, and the existing copies stay where they are

reading: A rectangular outline has one coloured cell in each inner corner. Each is erased and redrawn just outside the outline at the diagonally opposite corner, which is a point reflection through the outline's centre.

slots.subject: the 4 single cells in the inner corners of the outline
slots.target: the cell diagonally outside the outline at the opposite corner (point reflection through the outline centre)
slots.rest: inner corner cells cleared to background

why: the inner-corner colour at TL appears outside BR, TR outside BL, and so on; the interior becomes empty

reading: The most common colour stays. Every other cell becomes 5.
why: every non-background (non-majority) cell becomes 5; majority cells unchanged

reading: Each 2x2 grey block gets four single cells at its outside diagonal corners: 1 at top-left, 2 at top-right, 3 at bottom-left and 4 at bottom-right.
why: every 2x2 object has the same 4x4 pattern around it (1..2 / block / 3..4), and nothing else changes

reading: A grid of full grey separator lines is covered in noise of one colour c. All the noise is removed, the separator lines are restored to grey, and every crossing of a horizontal and a vertical separator becomes c.

slots.noise: all cells of the other non-background colour c
slots.rule: output = background, separator cells grey, separator crossings colour c

why: checked on all pairs: output is exactly 0 off the lines, 5 on the lines, and c at line crossings

reading: The output is twice as wide as the input. The horizontally periodic pattern band continues with its own period across the new width; it is not tiled as a block.

slots.unit: the smallest horizontal period of the coloured rows
slots.rule: each output cell (r, x) = input cell (r, x mod period)

why: each output row is its input row's periodic continuation; plain tiling fails on pairs with width not a multiple of the period
invariants: the input occupies the left half unchanged

reading: A lattice of 3x3 rings has two marks of a colour c for each colour present. The two marks give opposite corners of a rectangle snapped to the background lanes. The rectangle outline is drawn in c along the lanes, and the centre cell of every ring inside it becomes c.

slots.marks: pairs of same-colour cells off the 8 lattice
slots.rectangle: bounding box of the pair, expanded outward to the nearest background lanes
slots.draw: outline on the lanes in c; ring centres strictly inside become c

why: for every mark colour the outline lies on lane rows/columns through or just outside both marks, and only enclosed ring centres change

reading: Each non-background cell in the top row drops a full-height vertical line of its own colour. Where the line passes through a block of that same colour, the cells become background instead.
verb: drop lines, invert on same colour

slots.source: non-background cells of the top row
slots.line: the whole column below the source, to the bottom border
slots.colour: the source colour, except cells already of that colour become background

why: checked on all pairs: in each source column, cells equal to the source colour become background and all other cells become the source colour

reading: Two framed panels sit side by side and the right one is empty. Each shape in the left panel is copied to the same rows of the right panel, keeping its side margin. Shapes against the left side go left, shapes against the right side go right, and bars with a margin on both sides stretch across the full width.
verb: copy into panel, anchored and stretched

slots.source: contents of the left (non-empty) panel interior
slots.target: the empty right panel interior, same rows
slots.placement: keep distance to the nearer side wall; a shape with equal margins on both sides is stretched to keep both margins

why: every right-panel shape sits on the same rows as its source with the same left or right margin; full-span bars keep both margins
